lines.text: If you dig a hole on the beach to hide from warships, you'll lose it before the first wave is over. The sea floods in, and the walls cave in on top of you.
So you move up behind the dunes and pour concrete around your hole.
Now it's a lookout, but a grey box on a yellow beach is easy to spot, and one shell flattens it.
So you build the walls thicker than you are tall, and bury it under sand and grass like another dune.
Now it's a hideout, but tanks roll straight off the boats and up the sand.
So you weld steel beams into spiky crosses and scatter them everywhere. Czech hedgehogs. Tanks get stuck right on top of them.
Now it's a tank trap, but at high tide, the boats float right over them.
So you hammer wooden stakes into the shallows, with a mine on every tip. Boats blow open before they even land.
Running across open sand for ammo gets you shot, so you dig a tunnel back to camp.
And your window doesn't face the sea. It faces sideways, down the beach. The ships can't see it, but you can see every boat that lands. That's enfilade fire.
Add a stove, a deck of cards, and a seagull that steals your sandwich.
Congratulations. You've just built a piece of the Atlantic Wall.
